title: Analysis of the immune system under anti-IL17 therapy and correlation with treatment response in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa.
summary:
The main focus of this study is to analyze changes in the immune system and correlate them with the clinical response.
For this purpose, tissue and blood samples will be taken from 39 HS patients before starting treatment with an IL-17 antagonist. After 6 months, the patients can be divided into responders (HiSCR 75) and non-responders. Tissue from responders and non-responders is collected and subsequently analyzed. 
The interaction of innate immune cells will be investigated using various laboratory methods.
In addition, a mobile application will be used to track disease activity and response to treatment. Patients will document their condition weekly using the app, which includes skin images, pain questionnaires (VAS) and quality of life questionnaires (DLQI). This data will be correlated with clinical and immunological findings to determine factors for treatment success. 
The results should provide insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms that contribute to the different responses to IL-17 inhibitors in HS and ultimately lead to personalized treatment strategies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Ability to give informed consent, written consent to participate in the study
- Presence of at least two inflammatory inguinal HS nodules (lasting >12 weeks)
- Guideline-compliant indication for excision of the inguinal HS lesions with subsequent initiation of a biologic (IL-17 antagonist)
- Access to a smartphone
Exclusion criteria:
- Pre-therapy with biologics
- Immunosuppressive system therapies 
- Tumor disease 
- Contraindications for the initiation of IL-17 inhibitor therapy 
- Inability to give consent
- Age under 18 years
- No access to a smartphone 
- Malignancy in the last 5 years (epithelial skin tumors excluded)
- Pregnancy, breastfeeding, hereditary bleeding tendency
- Positive TB elispot
- Hepatitis or HIV
- chronic inflammatory bowel disease
- Alcohol dependence (score of ≥8 in the alcohol questionnaire)
